title: KEDA Kept Adding Pods for Traffic That Never Grew
description: 30 orders a second needs 3 pods. A SignalFlow query of total traffic made KEDA add pods up to 8; dividing that total by the pods reporting it kept 3, on EKS with Splunk Observability Cloud.
body:
My shop app took 30 orders a second, steady, start to finish. Each copy of the app can handle 10. So the right answer was 3 copies, and that's where I started.

KEDA, the tool scaling it, added 5 more anyway. The traffic never grew.

![Splunk Observability Cloud chart of shop pods running: 3 climbing to 8 in the two runs with the total query, staying at 3 in the two runs with the per-pod query](/abhimanyu/articles/keda-kept-adding-pods-for-traffic-that-never-grew/cover.png)

## The setup, in plain words

The app runs on Kubernetes, which runs copies of an app called pods. I used Amazon's managed Kubernetes (EKS) with two servers.

KEDA watches a number and tells Kubernetes how many pods to run. My number came from Splunk Observability Cloud, where OpenTelemetry sends every order the app takes. KEDA asks Splunk with a short SignalFlow query, compares the answer with a target of 10, and Kubernetes' autoscaler does the math:

pods wanted = pods now × (number from Splunk ÷ 10)

## The surprise

My first query asked Splunk for the **total** orders a second across all pods. That's 30 whether I run 3 pods or 8. So the math said 3 × 30 ÷ 10 = 9, and it kept asking for more until it hit my limit of 8 pods.

In both runs it reached 8 pods, at 120 s and 109 s. Splunk showed the same 30 orders a second spread over 8 pods: about 3.8 each. Five pods were there for traffic that never came.

![Splunk chart: orders per second across all pods stays near 30 in every run, while orders per pod drops to about 3.8 once the total query scales to 8 pods and stays near 10 with the per-pod query](/abhimanyu/articles/keda-kept-adding-pods-for-traffic-that-never-grew/step-1.png)

## The fix: ask for orders per pod

KEDA's Splunk trigger treats the query's answer as a plain value to hit, not as something it divides by pods itself. So the query has to do the dividing: the total, divided by the pods reporting it.

With 3 pods that's 30 ÷ 3 = 10, right on target, and the math says 3 × 10 ÷ 10 = 3. In both runs it stayed at 3 pods for the whole load (220 s and 219 s), and Splunk showed 10.1 orders a second per pod.

## What I took away

If a number drives your autoscaler, it has to go down when you add pods. Total traffic doesn't. Traffic per pod does.

## Try it yourself

You need an AWS account and a Splunk Observability Cloud org, with an ingest token for the Collector and an API token for KEDA. The lab code and the raw output of every run are in the [evidence folder](https://github.com/Abhimanyu9988/showmerit/tree/main/labs/keda-kept-adding-pods-for-traffic-that-never-grew/evidence).

The two SignalFlow queries KEDA runs (RUN is the lab's label on every series). Both count each pod's orders over the last 20 s, which keeps the answer the same whatever data resolution Splunk streams back. The total query:

```text
data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).sum().mean(over='30s').scale(0.05).publish()
```

The per-pod query divides that total by the pods that took orders in the last 20 s:

```text
(data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).sum().mean(over='30s').scale(0.05) / data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).count()).publish()
```

The trigger, with a 50 s scale-up window so one odd read can't add pods:

```yaml
triggers:
  - type: splunk-observability
    useCachedMetrics: true
    metadata:
      query: "QUERY"
      duration: "12"
      targetValue: "10"
      activationTargetValue: "1"
      queryAggregator: "latest"
    authenticationRef:
      name: splunk-keda
```

### Step 1: Create the cluster (terraform apply took 8m12s in my run)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Abhimanyu9988/showmerit.git
cd showmerit/labs/keda-kept-adding-pods-for-traffic-that-never-grew
export AWS_REGION=eu-central-1 LAB_NAME=keda-lab TF_VAR_lab_name=keda-lab
export SPLUNK_REALM=us1 SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-ingest-token SPLUNK_API_TOKEN=your-api-token
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
```

You get EKS 1.34 with two t3.large nodes.

### Step 2: The total query (717 s in my run)

Run `./reproduce.sh`. It installs the Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1 and KEDA 2.21.0, starts the shop app (Flask with zero-code OpenTelemetry 0.66b2) as a StatefulSet, warms all 8 pods once so each pod's series already exists in Splunk, then runs total-1 and total-2: 3 pods, 210 s of 30 orders a second.

### Step 3: The per-pod query (535 s in my run)

Run `./fix.sh`. Same load, same start of 3 pods, only the query changes. It runs perpod-1 and perpod-2 and reads all four runs back from Splunk.

| Run | Query | HPA target type | Most pods | Pods at end | Orders a second per pod in Splunk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| total-1 | total | Value | 8 | 8 | 3.8 |
| total-2 | total | Value | 8 | 8 | 3.7 |
| perpod-1 | per pod | Value | 3 | 3 | 10.1 |
| perpod-2 | per pod | Value | 3 | 3 | 10.1 |

## Clean up (the cluster costs money while it runs)

```bash
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

## What I didn't test

- **Scaling up from 1 pod** with the per-pod query: every run here starts at the 3 pods the load needs.
- **Scale-down**: each run ends while the load is still on.
- **Other loads and targets**: one app, one route, 30 orders a second, target 10.

## Sources

- [KEDA docs: Splunk Observability scaler (2.21)](https://keda.sh/docs/2.21/scalers/splunk-observability/)
- [KEDA issue 8297: the Splunk Observability scaler builds the HPA target as Value](https://github.com/kedacore/keda/issues/8297)
- [Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling, algorithm details](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/#algorithm-details)

source_replies.text: I measured this on EKS with KEDA 2.21.0. Starting from the 3 pods a fixed 30 requests a second needs (target 10), a SignalFlow query of the total request rate took the HPA to maxReplicaCount 8 in both runs, because the Value target compares the total. Dividing the same total by the pods reporting it (a count of the per-pod series in the same query) read 10 and the count stayed at 3 in both runs. I wrote up the full build here: {POST_URL}
